answers.cs_q1: I'm a college student studying communications, and I've worked part time at a grocery store for two years. I like helping people solve problems, and customer service lets me do that every day. I'm looking for a role where I can learn and grow.
answers.cs_q2: At the grocery store I work the service desk. I handle returns, answer questions, and help people who are confused about our rewards program. Last summer I also volunteered at a community help line, answering questions from neighbors.
answers.cs_q3: I try to listen first without interrupting. Then I say I understand why it's frustrating and that I want to fix it. I keep my voice slow and steady, and I focus on what I can do for them right now.
answers.cs_q4: First I'd let them explain and I'd apologize for the trouble, since it's their third call. Then I'd check the account notes so they don't repeat themselves. I'd run the tests I can, book a technician visit, and give them a ticket number and a time when I'll follow up.
answers.cs_q5: Once at work I gave a customer a refund for the wrong amount. I noticed it at the end of my shift, so I told my manager right away. I called the customer, apologized, and fixed the balance. Afterwards I started double checking every total before I close a return, and I haven't had that mistake again.
